prompt: Implement `parse_csv(text)` in csv_parser.py without using the csv module. It returns a list of rows, each a list of strings. Fields are separated by commas and records end with \n or \r\n. A final line ending doesn't add a row. Empty text gives []. A blank line in the middle gives the row [""]. A field starting with a double quote is quoted: it may contain commas and line endings, which are kept exactly, and "" inside it means one double quote. Raise ValueError if a quoted field is never closed, or if anything other than a comma or line ending follows its closing quote. A double quote in the middle of an unquoted field is an ordinary character. Spaces are kept.
